name: What happens if the renovation uncovers water damage or rot?

mainEntity.name: What should I do if demolition reveals water damage, rot, mold, or termite damage during a home renovation?
mainEntity.text: What should I do if demolition reveals water damage, rot, mold, or termite damage during a home renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: If demolition reveals water damage, rot, mold, or termite damage, the first step is to stop work in the affected area and document the condition before repairs begin. These problems often mean the renovation scope must expand to include drying, removal of damaged materials, framing or structural repair, and possibly pest or moisture remediation. In some cases, the issue also affects permits or inspections, especially if structural members are involved. Homeowners should expect the schedule and budget to shift once hidden damage is found. The best response is not panic, but a clear repair plan and a written change order that explains the extra work. A contractor experienced with older Los Angeles homes should be able to coordinate the next steps quickly and safely. Leaving damaged material in place or covering it over usually creates bigger problems later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stop work in the affected area, document the damage, and get a repair plan before continuing. Hidden damage often requires structural repair, drying, replacement of affected materials, and sometimes permit or inspection follow-up before finish work can resume.
